correctness.rationale: Every subalgebra is either U<=V or F_q(x+v)+W_j, with W_j unique J-stable j-plane. Mixed pair counts use subspace graphs over invariant W_l and exact Gaussian coefficient F. Two-outside pair counts follow from equality mod W_{max(j,k)+1} and the triangular multiplicities (2u-1). Pair types are exhaustive, yielding T and P. Degree comparison yields the three-part transition, and a direct independent brute-force original-bracket program checks every vector subspace and pair in nine small prime-field examples. These checks corroborate, not establish, the all-q proof.

value.rationale: Pairwise vector-sum closure is the defining subalgebra permutability statistic, distinct from counting subalgebras or elements. Its exact all-dimension incidence probability for a canonical family is useful to finite Lie-algebra lattice theory; a large-field 0, one-quarter, one transition across dimensions four, five and at least six is structurally meaningful and not automatic from the prior subalgebra-classification theorem. The argument isolates the new mixed-incidence and exterior-pair conditions.
